reason: Pancreatic sensing cells can respond to the elevated glucose in the post-meal blood.
expectation: The pancreatic cells will sense the glucose and trigger an insulin response.

effect: The meal's glucose first had to be linked to the whole body; I can now try the pancreatic sensing cells.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the intended sequence after my incorrect guess.
reason: Pancreatic cells should respond to the rising blood glucose in the body.
expectation: The pancreatic cells will detect the rise and release insulin.

effect: The pancreatic beta cells released insulin into blood, with routes toward muscle and liver.
reaction: The inset makes the signal's origin and destinations clear.
reason: The insulin route points toward skeletal muscle, where it can help cells take up glucose.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose uptake by muscle after the meal.

effect: Insulin helped muscle take up glucose, and the new goal shifts attention to maintaining blood glucose between meals.
reaction: The later inset usefully shows insulin release easing as blood glucose falls.
reason: Advancing time should establish the between-meal conditions before the liver responds.

choice.combine: Body taking up glucose into muscle

expectation: Blood glucose availability will decline as tissues use it and incoming glucose tapers.

effect: Blood glucose has fallen between meals while liver glycogen remains available.
reaction: The clock and vessel inset make the change in supply clear.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells include alpha cells, which may respond to falling glucose.
expectation: The pancreas will release glucagon, signalling the liver to make glucose available.

alternatives.reason: The liver has stored glycogen, but I expect a pancreatic signal first.

effect: Falling glucose prompted pancreatic alpha cells to release glucagon, with a blood route toward the liver.
reaction: The paired islet views make the contrast with insulin release clear.
reason: The glucagon route points to the liver, where stored glycogen can provide glucose between meals.
expectation: Glucagon will promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release into the blood.

effect: The liver released glucose from glycogen, and glucagon release decreased as blood glucose rose, completing the between-meal feedback response.
reaction: The sequential insets made the feedback loop clear and gave the chapter a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following falling glucose through glucagon release to liver glucose output was most worthwhile: the planned insets connect the signal, its target and the feedback response.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the meal's glucose to the body was necessary setup but less informative than the later regulation steps.

surprise.text: My first attempt to combine glucose-rich blood directly with pancreatic cells instead automatically linked it to the body, clarifying the intended sequence.

arbitrary.text: That initial requirement to attach the blood to the whole body before using the sensing cells was not obvious, although the compatibility feedback resolved it.

continue.text: I would continue: contrasting insulin and glucagon responses and seeing each signal ease as conditions change was a useful way to connect familiar biology to whole-body regulation.
